title: How did God make the world?
text: In the beginning there was nothing, and God made everything. On the first day He said, "Let there be light," and there was light. Then He made the sky, the sea and the dry land. He filled the land with plants and trees. He made the sun, the moon and the stars. He made fish for the sea and birds for the sky, and then animals on the land. On the sixth day God made people, Adam and Eve, and He loved them very much. God looked at everything and said it was very good. On the seventh day He rested. When you look at a flower or the stars, you can thank God who made them.

verse.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

title: Adam and Eve in the garden
text: God made Adam and Eve and put them in the beautiful Garden of Eden. They had everything they needed and they could talk with God. God asked them to obey one rule: do not eat the fruit of one special tree. But Eve and Adam listened to the serpent instead of God, and they ate it. They felt sorry and hid. God called, "Where are you?" because He still loved them. They had to leave the garden, but God did not forget them. He promised that one day a Savior would come. That Savior is Jesus Christ. This story teaches us to obey God, and to say sorry when we make a mistake.

verse.text: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?

title: Noah and the ark
text: Many people forgot God, but Noah loved Him and listened to Him. God told Noah to build a very big boat called an ark. Noah obeyed even though it took a long time. God told him to bring his family and two of every kind of animal into the ark. Then rain fell for many days and the earth was covered with water. Noah and everyone in the ark were safe because God took care of them. When the water went down, they came out. God put a rainbow in the sky and promised never to flood the whole earth again. When you see a rainbow, remember that God keeps His promises.

verse.text: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.

title: Abraham trusts God
text: Abraham was a man who trusted God completely. One day God told him to leave his home and go to a new land that God would show him. Abraham did not know the way, but he obeyed and took his wife Sarah and his family. God promised to make his family into a great nation, and that through his family all the world would be blessed. Abraham and Sarah waited many years, and in the end God gave them a son named Isaac. Abraham teaches us to trust God even when we cannot see the road ahead. The Church also remembers how Abraham welcomed three guests with kindness.

verse.text: And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

title: Joseph and his brothers
text: Joseph was the son of Jacob, and Jacob loved him very much. His brothers became jealous and sold him to travelers who took him to Egypt. Joseph was far from home, but God was with him. He worked hard and told the truth, even when it was hard. Later he helped Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to save food for seven years when there would be no rain. When Joseph became a leader in Egypt, his hungry brothers came to him for food. Joseph could have been angry, but he forgave them and took care of his whole family. Joseph teaches us to forgive, and to trust that God can turn bad things into good.

verse.text: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.

title: Baby Moses in the basket
text: The king of Egypt was unkind to God's people, the Israelites. A mother who loved her baby boy hid him for as long as she could. Then she made a little basket, put the baby inside, and placed it gently among the reeds by the river. His big sister Miriam stayed nearby to watch. The princess, the daughter of Pharaoh, came to the river and found the basket. She felt sorry for the baby and wanted to keep him. Miriam asked if she should find someone to care for him, and she brought the baby's own mother. The princess named him Moses. God took care of baby Moses, and He takes care of you too.

title: Moses and the burning bush
text: When Moses grew up, he looked after sheep in the desert. One day he saw a bush that was on fire, but the fire did not burn it up. Moses came closer. God spoke to him from the bush and told him to take off his shoes because he was standing on holy ground. God said He had seen how His people were suffering in Egypt, and He would send Moses to lead them out. Moses felt shy and afraid, but God promised, "I will be with you." The Church also sees the bush that burned but was not burned up as a sign of St. Mary, who carried God the Son and was not harmed.

verse.text: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM.

title: Moses, Pharaoh and the Red Sea
text: God sent Moses to ask Pharaoh to let the Israelites go free. Pharaoh said no again and again, so God showed His power with signs in Egypt. At last Pharaoh let the people go. They left in a hurry, but then Pharaoh changed his mind and his army chased them. The Israelites came to the Red Sea and were afraid. Moses told them not to be afraid. God opened a path through the sea, and the people walked across on dry ground with water like walls on both sides. They were safe on the other side, and they sang and thanked God. God rescues His people, and the Church sees the crossing as a sign of Baptism.

verse.text: The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

title: The Ten Commandments
text: After God freed the Israelites, they traveled to Mount Sinai. Moses went up the mountain and God gave him the Ten Commandments, written on two stone tablets. The first commandments teach us to love God: worship only Him, honor His name and keep His day holy. The others teach us to love people: honor your father and mother, do not kill, do not steal, do not lie, and do not wish for what belongs to others. The commandments are God's gift to show us how to live well. Jesus said they come down to two things: love God with all your heart, and love your neighbor as yourself.

verse.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

title: David and Goliath
text: The Philistine army had a giant soldier named Goliath. Every day he shouted at God's people and everyone was afraid. David was only a young shepherd boy, but he trusted God. He had already protected his sheep from a lion and a bear with God's help. David said he would fight Goliath. The king offered his armor, but it was too big, so David took only his sling and five smooth stones. David told Goliath that he came in the name of the Lord. With one stone from his sling, David defeated the giant. Later David became king of Israel. Even when we feel small, God can help us do great things.

verse.text: the battle is the LORD's

title: Daniel in the lions' den
text: Daniel loved God and prayed three times every day. Some men in the land of Babylon were jealous of him. They tricked the king, Darius, into making a rule that no one could pray to anyone but the king. Daniel kept praying to God anyway. The king was sad, but the rule had to be kept, and Daniel was put into a den full of lions. The king could not sleep all night. In the morning he hurried to the den and called out to Daniel. Daniel answered that God had sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths. Daniel was safe. We can be brave and keep praying, because God is always with us.

verse.text: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths

title: Jonah and the big fish
text: God asked Jonah to go to the city of Nineveh and tell the people to stop doing wrong. Jonah did not want to go, so he got on a ship going the other way. God sent a great storm. Jonah knew it was because of him, and he asked the sailors to throw him into the sea. The storm stopped. God sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and he stayed inside for three days and three nights. Jonah prayed and said sorry, and the fish put him on dry land. This time Jonah obeyed and went to Nineveh. The people listened and turned back to God, and God forgave them. God is kind and forgives when we say sorry.

verse.text: Salvation is of the LORD.

title: Queen Esther
text: Esther was a young Jewish woman who became queen of Persia. Her cousin Mordecai had raised her, and he told her to be careful and not to tell the king that she was Jewish. A proud man named Haman made a plan to harm the Jewish people. Mordecai asked Esther to speak to the king. It was dangerous to go to the king without being called, but Esther was brave. She asked the people to fast and pray for three days, and then she went to the king. God helped her, and the king listened and saved her people. Esther teaches us to pray, to be brave, and to help others when God gives us a chance.

verse.text: who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

title: The angel visits Mary and Jesus is born
text: In the town of Nazareth lived a young woman named Mary. The angel Gabriel came to her and said that God had chosen her to be the mother of Jesus, the Son of God. Mary was surprised, but she trusted God and said, "Let it be to me according to your word." We call her the Theotokos, the Mother of God. Before Jesus was born, Mary and Joseph traveled to Bethlehem. There was no room for them at the inn, so Jesus was born in a stable and laid in a manger. Angels told shepherds nearby the good news, and the shepherds hurried to see the baby. Jesus is the Savior God sent to the world.

verse.text: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.

title: The wise men and the star
text: After Jesus was born, wise men from the east saw a special star. They knew it meant that a great King had been born, so they traveled a long way to find Him. They went to Jerusalem and asked where the baby was. King Herod was jealous and wanted to harm the child, but the wise men did not tell him where Jesus was. The star led them to Bethlehem. When they saw Jesus with Mary His mother, they bowed down and worshiped Him. They gave Him gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh. God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they went home another way.

verse.text: Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.

title: The baptism of Jesus
text: When Jesus grew up, He went to the Jordan River where John the Baptist was baptizing people. Jesus asked John to baptize Him. John was surprised, but he did it. When Jesus came up out of the water, the heavens opened. The Holy Spirit came down on Jesus like a dove, and the voice of God the Father spoke from heaven, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." In this one moment we see all three Persons of the Holy Trinity. The Church celebrates this on the Feast of Theophany, and it shows us that our own Baptism is a special gift from God.

verse.text: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

title: Jesus calls His disciples
text: One day Jesus was walking by the Sea of Galilee. He saw two brothers, Simon, who was later called Peter, and Andrew. They were fishermen casting their nets. Jesus said, "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men." They left their nets and followed Him right away. Jesus then called two more brothers, James and John, who were also fishermen. Later He chose twelve disciples, also called apostles, to be with Him and learn from Him. After the Resurrection, they went out and told the world about Jesus. They were ordinary people, and Jesus can use anyone who is willing to say yes when He calls.

verse.text: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

title: Jesus feeds the five thousand
text: A very large crowd followed Jesus to hear Him teach, and the day grew late. The people were hungry. The disciples found one boy who had five small barley loaves and two little fish. Jesus took the boy's lunch, looked up to heaven and thanked God. Then He broke the bread and gave it to the disciples to share. Everyone ate until they were full, about five thousand men, besides women and children. Afterward the disciples gathered twelve baskets of leftovers. This miracle shows that Jesus cares when we are hungry, and that when we share what we have, God can make it enough.

verse.text: I am the bread of life

title: Jesus calms the storm
text: One evening Jesus and His disciples got into a boat to cross the lake. Jesus was tired and fell asleep. Suddenly a big storm came, the waves were high and water filled the boat. The disciples were very scared and woke Jesus up. Jesus stood up and said to the wind and the sea, "Peace, be still." At once the wind stopped and everything was calm. Jesus asked the disciples why they had so little faith. They were amazed that even the wind and the sea obey Him. When you are scared, you can pray, because Jesus is with you in every storm.

verse.text: Peace, be still.

title: The good Samaritan
text: Jesus told a story about a man who was hurt by robbers on the road and left on the ground. A priest walked past without helping. Another man from the temple saw him and also walked by. Then a Samaritan came. Samaritans and Jews did not usually get along, but this man stopped. He cleaned and bandaged the wounds, put the man on his own donkey, took him to an inn and paid for his care. Jesus asked who was a neighbor to the hurt man. The answer was, the one who showed mercy. Jesus told us to go and do the same. Our neighbor is anyone who needs our help.

verse.text: Go, and do thou likewise.

title: The prodigal son
text: Jesus told a story about a father with two sons. The younger son asked for his share of the money, left home and spent it all on foolish things. Soon he was hungry and had nothing. He decided to go back home and say sorry. While he was still far away, his father saw him, ran to him and hugged him. The son said he was sorry, and the father welcomed him and gave a big party. The father in the story is like God. God is always ready to welcome us back when we say sorry. The Church reads this story on one of the Sundays of Great Lent, as a picture of repentance and of the joy in heaven when someone comes back to God.

verse.text: But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

title: The lost sheep
text: Jesus told a story about a shepherd with a hundred sheep. One day one sheep wandered away and got lost. The shepherd left the other ninety-nine and went to look for the lost one. He searched and searched until he found it. He was so happy that he put the sheep on his shoulders and carried it home. Then he called his friends and said, "Rejoice with me, I have found my sheep!" Jesus is the Good Shepherd, and we are His sheep. He loves every one of us, and when we are lost or sad He comes looking for us.

verse.text: Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.

title: The Last Supper
text: On the night before His crucifixion, Jesus ate a special meal with His twelve disciples. During the meal He took bread, thanked God, broke it and gave it to them, saying it was His body. Then He took the cup of wine and said it was His blood, given for many. He told them to do this in remembrance of Him. The Church believes that Jesus gave us the Holy Eucharist at this supper, and we celebrate it in every Holy Liturgy. Jesus also washed His disciples' feet to show that those who love Him must serve others with humility. We remember this on Holy Thursday.

verse.text: This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

title: Jesus dies on the cross and rises again
text: Jesus loves us so much that He gave His life for us. On Good Friday He was nailed to the cross and He died, so that our sins could be forgiven. This is a very sad day, but it is also the day He saved us. His friends placed His body in a tomb. On the third day, early on Sunday morning, some women went to the tomb and found it empty. An angel told them, "He is risen." Jesus appeared to His disciples and they were filled with joy. Jesus defeated death and gives us new life. We celebrate this every Sunday, and especially on the Feast of the Resurrection.

verse.text: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.

title: Pentecost: the Holy Spirit comes
text: After Jesus rose from the dead and went up to heaven, He told His disciples to wait in Jerusalem for the gift of the Holy Spirit. They gathered together, with St. Mary and others, and prayed. On the day of Pentecost, a sound like a strong wind filled the house, and what looked like flames rested on each of them. They were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, so people from many countries could hear about Jesus in their own language. That day about three thousand people were baptized. We call Pentecost the birthday of the Church.

verse.text: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

title: The conversion of St. Paul
text: Saul was a man who did not believe in Jesus, and he was unkind to the early Christians. One day he was traveling to the city of Damascus when a bright light from heaven shone around him and he fell to the ground. A voice said, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" It was Jesus. Saul could not see. His companions led him into the city, where a faithful man named Ananias prayed for him. Saul could see again, and he was baptized. He became Paul, a great apostle who traveled to many places and wrote letters that are now part of the New Testament. Jesus can change anyone's heart.

verse.text: Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

title: What does Theotokos mean?
text: Theotokos is a Greek word. "Theo" means God and "tokos" means one who bears, so it means "she who bore God," or the Mother of God. The Church gives this title to St. Mary, the Virgin Mary, because the Child she carried and gave birth to is Jesus Christ, who is truly God and truly man. So the title is really about Jesus first. The Bible shows this when Elizabeth greeted Mary as "the mother of my Lord" (Luke 1:43). When you hear Theotokos in a hymn or prayer, remember that St. Mary is the mother who loved Jesus, and she is honored by the whole Church.

title: What does Pascha mean?
text: Pascha comes from a Hebrew word that means Passover. Long ago, God saved His people from Egypt on the night of the Passover lamb. In the Church, Pascha is the name of Holy Week, when we remember how Jesus gave His life on the cross to save us and to lift us up to heaven. Holy Week has special services, and the church is quiet and serious. Orthodox Christians also use the word Pascha for the joyful feast of the Resurrection instead of the word Easter. Pascha reminds us that Jesus, our true Passover, saves us and brings us from sadness to joy.

title: What is the Agpeya?
text: The Agpeya is the Coptic Orthodox prayer book. Its name comes from a Coptic word that means "hour," so it is often called the Book of Hours. It has seven prayer times: Prime in the morning, the Third, Sixth and Ninth hours during the day, the Eleventh hour at sunset, the Twelfth hour at bedtime, and the Midnight prayer. A special Veil prayer is for priests and monks. Each hour has psalms, a reading from the Gospel and short prayers, and each one reminds us of something Jesus did for us. The Agpeya helps us talk with God through the whole day, and kids can start with the morning and bedtime prayers.

title: What does Hosanna mean?
text: Hosanna is a Hebrew word that means "save us," and it also became a shout of joy and praise. On Palm Sunday, Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey. Crowds spread branches and cloaks on the road and shouted "Hosanna to the Son of David!" They welcomed Him as their King. Today we sing Hosanna in the Church on Palm Sunday, holding palm leaves and crosses in a procession. It reminds us to welcome Jesus into our hearts with joy. He is the one who really saves us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.

title: What does Alleluia mean?
text: Alleluia, also written Hallelujah, is a Hebrew word that means "praise the Lord." It is a joyful word that we use to thank and praise God. In the Church we sing Alleluia in prayers, hymns and spiritual songs. The Bible shows that the angels and saints in heaven praise God with this same word (Revelation 19:1). So when we sing Alleluia in church, we join the heavenly creatures in their praise. In the Psalms, people also call out Alleluia to praise God for His great love. You can sing Alleluia any time you feel happy and thankful.

verse.text: Praise ye the LORD. Praise the LORD, O my soul.

title: What does Kyrie eleison mean?
text: Kyrie eleison is Greek. It means "Lord, have mercy." It is a very old short prayer that the Church says or sings in worship. We say it again and again in the Agpeya, where each hour has it many times, and also in the Holy Liturgy. When we say it, we ask God for His kindness and help, for ourselves, for our family, for the sick and sad, and for the whole world. It is short and simple, so kids can pray it quietly any time, for example when they feel worried, when they have done something wrong, or when they know someone who needs help.

title: What does Amen mean?
text: Amen is a word we say at the end of a prayer. It means "so be it" or "let it be so." When we say Amen, we are agreeing with what was prayed and making the prayer our own. That is why people in church say it after prayers and blessings. Even though it is a tiny word, it is important, because it shows that we mean what we prayed and that we trust God to hear us. Next time you say Amen at the end of a prayer, say it clearly and slowly, and think about the words you just prayed. Amen helps all of us pray together.

title: What does the word iconostasis mean?
text: The iconostasis is a wooden or marble stand that holds holy icons in a Coptic church. It stands in front of the altar area. It has three doors, and the middle one, called the Royal Door, leads to the main altar. On one side of the Royal Door we see the icon of our Lord Jesus, and on the other side the icon of St. Mary. More icons of saints and angels are placed around them. The icons remind us that the saints and the angels are with us when we praise God. They are not a wall that keeps people away. They help us remember Jesus and His friends while we pray.

title: What is the Korban?
text: Korban means "offering." It is the special bread that the church uses for the Holy Liturgy, also called the Eucharistic bread. It is a small round loaf made from fine wheat flour, water and yeast, with no salt. Before it is baked, it is stamped with a design. In the middle is a part called the Despatikon, which means "lordly," with twelve crosses around it for the twelve apostles. It also has five small holes that remind us of the nails and the spear, and the word "holy" three times. In the Liturgy, this bread becomes the Body of Christ. That is why we treat it with great respect.

title: The Lord's Prayer
text: The Lord's Prayer is the prayer Jesus Himself taught His disciples. We pray it in the Agpeya, in the Holy Liturgy and every day. In the Coptic Church we say it like this: "Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil, in Christ Jesus our Lord. For Thine is the kingdom, the power and the glory, forever. Amen." In this prayer we praise God, ask for what we need and ask Him to forgive us.
kw: our father who art in heaven

title: The Trisagion prayer
text: The Trisagion is a Greek word that means "Thrice Holy," because we say "holy" three times. It is a short hymn that the Church sings and prays in its services, and it is chanted in all our liturgies. We say: "Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, who was crucified for us, have mercy on us." In the Coptic Church, the whole hymn is a prayer to Jesus Christ. The three holies also remind us of the Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and we join the angels in praising God as holy. When you pray, you can say the Trisagion slowly to remember how great and kind God is.

title: Psalm 23: The Lord is my shepherd
text: Psalm 23 was written by King David, who had been a shepherd boy. It says that God takes care of us like a shepherd cares for his sheep. "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever."

title: A simple morning prayer
text: When we wake up, we can thank God for a new day. Here is a simple prayer you can say: "Thank You, God, for this new day. Thank You for keeping me safe all night. Please be with me today, at home and at school. Help me to be kind, to tell the truth and to obey. Bless my family and my friends. Keep me in Your love. Amen." You can make the sign of the cross before you pray. Praying in the morning helps us remember that God is with us all day long. When you are older, you can learn the Agpeya morning prayer, called Prime.

title: A simple evening prayer
text: At the end of the day, we can say thank you to God before we sleep. Here is a simple prayer: "Thank You, Jesus, for today. Thank You for my family, my food and my friends. I am sorry for the things I did wrong today. Please forgive me and help me do better. Keep me safe while I sleep, and send Your angels to guard me. Bless everyone I love. Amen." You can make the sign of the cross and lie down in peace, knowing God watches over you. The Agpeya also has special prayers for sunset, bedtime and midnight when you are ready to learn them.

title: A prayer before a meal
text: Before we eat, we stop and thank God for our food. God gives us everything we have, and we say thank you just like we thank someone for a gift. Here is a simple prayer: "Thank You, God, for this food. Thank You for the people who made it. Bless it and bless us. Help us to share with others who are hungry. Amen." The Church also has a grace prayer in the Agpeya for meals. We can make the sign of the cross before eating, and after the meal we say thank you again. Remember that many people in the world do not have enough food, so we pray for them as well.

title: A prayer for other people
text: We can pray for other people, because God listens and loves them too. The Bible tells us to pray for each other. Here is a simple prayer: "Lord Jesus, please bless my mom and dad, my family and my friends. Please help those who are sick and comfort those who are sad. Help people who are hungry or alone. Please take care of our priest, our Pope and our church. Help me to be a good friend to everyone. Amen." You can add the names of people you want to pray for. When we pray for others we show love, and it makes our own heart kinder.

title: How do we pray the Agpeya?
text: Each hour of the Agpeya follows a pattern, so it becomes easy to learn. We begin with an introduction that includes the Lord's Prayer, then the Prayer of Thanksgiving and Psalm 50, which asks God for mercy. After that we pray the psalms for that hour and a short reading from the Gospel. Then come short prayers for the needs of the world, and we say "Lord, have mercy" forty-one times. The hour ends with more short prayers. We do not need to hurry. We can pray a little at a time, and a parent or a servant can help us find the place in the book. The Agpeya teaches us to talk to God all through the day.

title: When do we pray the Agpeya hours?
text: The Agpeya has prayers for seven times in the day and night. Prime, the first hour, is at about 6 in the morning, and it celebrates the Resurrection and the new light. The Third hour, about 9 in the morning, remembers the Holy Spirit coming down on the apostles. The Sixth hour, at noon, remembers Jesus on the cross. The Ninth hour, about 3 in the afternoon, remembers Jesus dying for us and the thief who repented. The Eleventh hour, at sunset, remembers Jesus' body being taken down from the cross. The Twelfth hour, at bedtime, remembers His burial. The Midnight prayer reminds us that Jesus will come again. You can start with one or two hours.

title: What does it mean to love like Jesus?
text: Jesus said that the most important thing we can do is love God and love other people. His love is kind and gives. Jesus loved us so much that He died for us on the cross. We can love like Jesus when we share our toys and food, help a friend who is sad, listen to our parents and teachers, and are kind even to people who are not kind to us. Love is more than words, it is what we do. When we love others, we show them the love of God, and our hearts become full of joy.

verse.text: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you

title: Being kind
text: Being kind means treating other people the way we like to be treated. A kind person shares, says nice words, helps others and does not make fun of anyone. We can be kind at home, at school and at church. We can help a younger child, include someone who is alone, or say please and thank you. Kindness does not have to be big. Small things matter to God. Jesus was always kind to everyone, to children, to people who were sick, and even to people who were rude to Him. When we are kind, we become more like Jesus.

verse.text: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.

title: Forgiving others
text: To forgive means to let go of anger when someone hurts us, and to give them another chance. It can be hard, but Jesus teaches us to forgive. Jesus forgave the people who nailed Him to the cross. God forgives us when we are sorry, so we should forgive others too. In the Lord's Prayer we ask God to forgive us as we forgive others. Forgiving does not mean that what happened was okay. It means we choose peace over being angry. If we are hurt, we can tell a parent or a teacher, and we can pray for the person who hurt us.

verse.text: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.

title: Telling the truth
text: Honesty means telling the truth, even when it is hard. God loves the truth, and Jesus is called the Truth. When we make a mistake, it is better to say what happened and say sorry than to lie. Lying can hurt people and breaks trust. Telling the truth makes our hearts light and makes people trust us. Being honest also means not cheating on a test or taking something that is not ours. If you made a mistake and feel afraid, you can pray and ask God for courage. Parents and teachers are usually happy when we are honest, even if we did something wrong.

verse.text: Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight.

title: Saying thank you to God
text: Gratitude means being thankful. Everything we have comes from God: our family, our food, our home, our friends, and even the air we breathe. When we say thank you to God, we remember how good He is. In the Holy Liturgy and in the Agpeya, we begin many prayers with thanksgiving. We can thank God every day when we wake up, before we eat and before we go to sleep. We can also thank people who help us, like parents, teachers and friends. A thankful heart is a happy heart, and it helps us not to complain.

verse.text: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

title: Who is the Holy Trinity?
text: We believe in one God who is three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. This is called the Holy Trinity. The three Persons are not three different gods. They are one God, equal and always together, and they love each other perfectly. We cannot fully understand this with our minds, because God is much bigger than we are. But we know it because Jesus taught us. When we make the sign of the cross we say, In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, one God. We are baptized in the name of the Trinity, and we end our prayers with glory to the Trinity.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost

title: How can God be three and one?
text: This is a big question, and even grown ups cannot fully explain it. God is a mystery, which means He is so great that our minds cannot hold all of Him. The Church teaches that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three Persons who share one nature, so they are one God. The Father is the source, the Son is born of the Father before all time, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father. Some people use pictures to help, like the sun with its light and its heat, but every picture is small compared to God. The best thing we can do is pray, thank God, and ask Abouna when we wonder.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who is Jesus?
text: Jesus is the Son of God. He is God and He is also truly a human being. Long ago, God the Son came down from heaven to be born of the Virgin Mary so that He could save us. He grew up, taught people, healed the sick and loved everyone. Then He died on the cross for us and rose again on the third day. Now He is alive and always with us. Jesus is our Savior and our friend. When we pray, we are talking to Him. He loves every child very much, and He knows each of us by name.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

title: What is the Incarnation?
text: The Incarnation means that God the Son became a man. The word comes from a word for flesh. Jesus took a real human body and soul from the Virgin Mary by the work of the Holy Spirit, and He stayed fully God at the same time. He did not stop being God when He became human. We celebrate this at the feast of the Nativity. The Church teaches that He is one Christ, perfect God and perfect man, joined together without mixing or change. He became like us so that He could heal us, forgive us and bring us back to God. It is the greatest sign of God's love.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us

title: Who is St. Mary, the Theotokos?
text: St. Mary is the Virgin who gave birth to Jesus. We call her the Theotokos, a Greek word that means the Mother of God, because the baby she carried is God the Son. She said yes to God with a humble heart. She is the most blessed of all women, and the Church honors her more than all the saints. We love her like a spiritual mother and we ask for her prayers. We do not worship her, we worship only God. In church you will see her icon near the front, and we sing her praises often.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we honor St. Mary so much?
text: We honor St. Mary because God chose her to be the mother of Jesus, and she was humble and obedient. When the angel Gabriel told her the news, she answered that she was the handmaid of the Lord. Elizabeth called her blessed among women, and Mary herself said that all generations would call her blessed. Honoring her does not take anything away from Jesus. It is a way of honoring Him, because she is His mother. We ask for her prayers the way we ask a friend or family member to pray for us. The Coptic Church has many hymns and feasts for her, and she is a great example of faith and kindness.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who is the Holy Spirit?
text: The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Holy Trinity. He is God, equal with the Father and the Son. We believe that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father, and in the Creed we call Him the Lord and Giver of Life. The Holy Spirit comes down on us in baptism and in the sacraments. He helps us to love God, to understand the Bible, to pray and to do what is right. On the day of Pentecost He came upon the apostles like a rushing wind and tongues of fire. The Holy Spirit is our Comforter and helper, and He is always near to us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Baptism
text: Baptism is the first sacrament. In baptism a person is dipped three times in water in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. It is like being born again as a child of God. Our sins are washed away and we become members of the Church, the family of God. In the Coptic Church babies are usually baptized, and the priest holds them and dips them in the water. A person is baptized only once in their life. After baptism comes chrismation with the holy oil. Jesus Himself was baptized in the Jordan River, and He told His disciples to baptize all nations.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost

title: Chrismation (Holy Myron)
text: Right after baptism comes the sacrament of Chrismation. The priest anoints the newly baptized person with the Holy Myron, a special blessed oil. The Myron is made from olive oil mixed with sweet spices, and the Church also uses it in baptism and when a church building or its holy vessels are blessed. Through this anointing we receive the Holy Spirit living in us. It also strengthens us, and after it we have the right to receive Holy Communion. The Church has used holy anointing oil since the Old Testament, when God told Moses to prepare it for priests and kings. Chrismation is received one time, just like baptism. Ask Abouna if you would like to know more about how it is made.

title: Confession and repentance
text: Confession is the sacrament where we tell our sins to God in front of a priest, and the priest prays the prayer of absolution. This means God forgives us through the Church. We are sorry for what we did wrong, we promise to try again, and we leave with a clean heart. It is not meant to scare us. Confession is like a doctor's visit for the soul, and the priest is a loving father who helps us. We can go to confession many times, and it is a good idea to go regularly, especially before Holy Communion. Ask Abouna when you are ready and how to prepare.
kw: tell my sins to the priest
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

title: The Eucharist (Holy Communion)
text: The Eucharist is the sacrament where we receive the Body and Blood of Jesus Christ. At the Holy Liturgy, the bread and wine are changed by the Holy Spirit into the true Body and Blood of our Lord. We do not just remember Jesus, we receive Him. Jesus began this at the Last Supper when He gave His disciples bread and wine and told them to do this in remembrance of Him. Communion gives us forgiveness, strength and life with God. The word Eucharist means thanksgiving. We prepare for it by confessing, fasting before it, and coming with a clean heart and respect.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever

title: Matrimony (marriage)
text: Matrimony is the sacrament of marriage. A man and a woman are joined together in front of God and the Church, and the priest prays over them and puts crowns on their heads. The crowns remind us of the joy of the new family and of the crown of the martyrs, which means loving and sacrificing for one another. The couple promise to love each other and to stay together, and God blesses their home. In the Coptic Church, a marriage is a holy path to heaven for both of them, and children are a gift from God. Kids can pray for their parents and family every day.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Priesthood (ordination)
text: Priesthood is the sacrament where a man is set apart to serve God and the Church. The bishop lays his hands on him and prays, and the Holy Spirit gives him the grace to serve. There are three ranks: the deacon, the priest and the bishop. A priest can pray the Holy Liturgy, baptize, hear confessions and bless. He is a shepherd who takes care of God's people, like a father in the family. In the Coptic Church the priest is called Abouna, which means our father. We respect our priests, we pray for them, and we help them in the church. A man is ordained only once for each rank.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Unction of the Sick
text: The sacrament of the Unction of the Sick is for people who are ill. The priest prays over blessed oil and anoints the sick person with it, and the family prays together with him. We ask God to heal the person in body and soul and to forgive their sins. This comes from the letter of St. James, who told the sick to call for the priests of the church to pray and anoint with oil in the name of the Lord. In this sacrament seven lamps are lit during the prayers. The Church teaches that God is the One who gives the cure, and we trust His love in every case. If someone in your family is sick, you can ask Abouna to visit and pray. Kids can pray for the sick too, and send them a kind card or a call.

title: What is the Holy Liturgy?
text: The Holy Liturgy is our main worship service. It is the prayer where we gather as God's family to praise Him, hear His Word and receive Holy Communion. We usually have it on Sunday mornings, and on feast days too. Everyone takes part, with the priest, the deacons and the people singing and answering together. It can feel long, but it is the most beautiful time of the week, because heaven and earth are joined together and the angels worship with us. Coming to the Liturgy every Sunday helps us grow close to Jesus and to each other.
kw: why do we go to church
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Liturgy in simple steps
text: The Holy Liturgy has main parts. First is the offering of the bread and wine, and the prayers of preparation. Then comes the Liturgy of the Word, with readings from the Bible, like the Epistles and the Gospel, and the priest often gives a sermon. After that comes the Liturgy of the Faithful, where we say the Creed and the priest prays over the bread and wine. The Holy Spirit changes them into the Body and Blood of Christ. The service ends with Holy Communion, the thanksgiving and the blessing. There are many hymns, prayers and responses along the way, and everyone takes part.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What do we do during the Liturgy?
text: During the Liturgy we do not just watch, we pray and sing together. We stand when the Gospel is read, because we are listening to Jesus. We say the responses, like Amen and Lord have mercy. We listen quietly to the readings and the sermon. When it is time for Communion, those who are prepared line up with respect and receive it. At the end we receive the blessing and go home in peace. Little ones can follow along by singing, watching the deacons, looking at the icons, and sitting still. If you do not understand something, you can ask Abouna or a servant after church.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The church door and the nave
text: When you walk into a Coptic church, you first come to the narthex and the main hall, called the nave. This is where the people stand and pray. The church is a house of God, so we enter with respect, making the sign of the cross and sometimes kissing the cross or the icons. The nave faces east, because Christ is the Sun of Righteousness. The nave represents the earth, where we the people worship God together. The door reminds us that Jesus said He is the door, and we enter into His family through Him. We walk in quietly and keep our voices low.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Haykal?
text: The Haykal is the sanctuary, the most holy part of the church. It is where the altar stands, and it is where the priest and deacons serve the Holy Liturgy. The Haykal reminds us of heaven, where God's throne is. Because it is so holy, only the clergy and those who have a blessing to serve there go in, and we do not enter the Haykal unless Abouna says it is okay. Moses once had to take off his shoes because he stood on holy ground, and this reminds us to be very respectful in holy places. When the curtain opens during the Liturgy, we stay still and look toward the altar with love.

title: What is the iconostasis?
text: The iconostasis is the stand of icons in front of the Haykal. Its name means a stand for icons, and it is made of wood or marble. It has three doors, and the middle one is called the Royal Door, which leads to the altar. On one side of the Royal Door you will see the icon of Jesus Christ, and on the other side the icon of the Virgin Mary. There are also icons of angels and saints. The iconostasis does not shut us out from God. It reminds us that the saints and heavenly creatures are with us, joining us in praising God. You can look at the icons and say a little prayer to each saint.

title: The altar
text: The altar is the holy table in the middle of the Haykal, the sanctuary. It is the most important place in the church, because this is where the Holy Sacrifice is offered, and the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Jesus during the Holy Liturgy. Four pillars stand around it with a little dome above, called a canopy. The altar reminds us of the tomb of the Lord Jesus Christ, where His body was laid, and it also reminds us of the cross where He gave Himself for us. Because it is so holy, we treat it with great respect, and we only go near it when Abouna says it is okay.

title: Domes and the cross on the church
text: Many Coptic churches have domes on the roof and a cross on top. The dome reminds us of heaven above us, and the church seems to point us up to God. The cross on the top shows that this building belongs to Jesus Christ who died and rose for us, and everyone passing by can see it. Inside the dome there is sometimes an icon of Christ. The church building is shaped to teach us, with the nave for the people, the Haykal for the altar, and the dome and cross pointing to heaven. Whenever you see a cross on a church, you can make the sign of the cross.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we have icons?
text: Icons are holy pictures of Jesus, the Virgin Mary, the angels and the saints. We do not worship icons. We worship only God. We honor the icons, which is a way of honoring the ones they show, like kissing a photo of someone we love. The icons around us remind us that the saints and the heavenly beings are with us, joining us in praising God, and that the saints are alive in Christ and pray for us. Icons help us remember their stories. In church you will see icons on the iconostasis and in many places on the walls. You can look at them and say a little prayer to each saint.

title: Why do we use incense?
text: We use incense in church because it is a sign of prayer going up to God. Incense is a sweet mixture of gums, resin and spices that is burned in worship. The Psalms say, Let my prayer be set before You as incense. In the Old Testament, incense was burned in the temple, and in the Book of Revelation the heavenly priests hold golden censers full of incense. The censer is the metal container that holds the burning coals, and the priest and deacons use it to cense the altar, the icons and the people. As the little pieces of incense burn and give off their sweet smell, they remind us to give ourselves to God in prayer.

title: Why do we light candles?
text: When we light a candle in church, it is a small prayer. The light reminds us that Jesus is the Light of the world, and that we should shine for Him. The candle burns up while giving light, which teaches us to give ourselves to God and others. People often light a candle in front of an icon, asking God and the saints to pray for a need, or to say thank you. The candle itself does not do the magic, the prayer does. When you light one, make the sign of the cross, say a short prayer, and be careful with the fire. Always ask an adult to help you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The sign of the cross
text: The sign of the cross is a prayer we make with our hand. We touch our forehead and our chest, and then we cross over our shoulders, while saying, In the name of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one God. Amen. We remember that Jesus died on the cross for us, and we say that we belong to the Holy Trinity. We make it when we begin to pray, when we eat, when we pass a church, before a test and when we are afraid. It is a small way to ask for God's help. Ask Abouna or a servant to show you how to make it, and they will help you practice.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Standing, kneeling and prostrations
text: In church our body prays along with our heart. We stand to praise God and when the Gospel is read, because we stand when someone important is speaking. We bow our heads and sometimes kneel to say sorry and to ask for mercy. A prostration, called a metanoia, is when we kneel and touch the ground with our head or hands, showing humility and worship to God alone. In the Coptic Church we usually do not kneel during the Liturgy on Sundays or during the fifty days after Easter, because those are days of joy. During Lent and the Agpeya we use prostrations more. Follow the deacon, and ask Abouna if you are unsure.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is a deacon?
text: A deacon is a servant of the church. The word deacon means servant. Deacons help the priest during the Holy Liturgy by reading the Bible, singing the hymns, leading the prayers and helping with the altar. In the Coptic Church, boys and men can be ordained as deacons, and there are different ranks. Many children start serving as young deacons and learn the hymns in Coptic and Arabic or English. The first deacons in the Bible were chosen by the apostles to help serve, and one of them was St. Stephen. Deacons wear a white tunic with a colored stole, and they serve with joy and with respect.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What does a priest do?
text: A priest is a servant of God and a shepherd of His people. In the Coptic Church we call him Abouna, which means our father. The priest serves the Holy Liturgy, prays the prayers of the church, baptizes, gives Holy Communion, hears confessions, blesses marriages and visits the sick. He is ordained by a bishop. Priests can be married if they were married before they were ordained, which is common in our church. A priest loves the people of his church like his own family and prays for us each day. When you meet Abouna, you can ask him for a blessing, and you can ask him any question about God and the church.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Bishops and the Pope
text: A bishop is the leader of a diocese, which is a group of churches in one region, and priests serve under their bishop. Above the bishops, the Pope of Alexandria is the head of the whole Coptic Orthodox Church. His title is the Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St. Mark, and he is the successor of St. Mark, who founded our church. The word patriarch means a father and a leader. In the earliest times the head of the church was the bishop of Alexandria, who was called Pope, a word that also means father. We pray for our Pope and our bishops by name, and we ask Abouna to teach us more about how the church is led.

title: Who is the Pope of Alexandria?
text: The Pope of Alexandria is the spiritual father and the head of the Coptic Orthodox Church. His title is the Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St. Mark, because he is the successor of St. Mark, who founded our church in Egypt. The word pope means father, and the word patriarch means a father and a leader. He leads the bishops, and the bishops and priests serve under his care. We remember him in our prayers, and we ask God to keep him safe and wise. You can ask Abouna for the name of the current Pope.

title: St. Mark the Apostle, founder of our church
text: St. Mark the Apostle brought the Gospel to Egypt and founded the Church of Alexandria, which is why we are called the Church of St. Mark. He wrote the Gospel of Mark, and our Church counts him among the seventy apostles. He also helped other apostles like St. Peter, St. Paul and St. Barnabas. In Alexandria he preached about Jesus, and many people believed and were baptized. He became the first Pope of Alexandria, and he is remembered as a martyr who gave his life for Jesus there. His martyrdom is remembered in the Church on 30 Baramoudah. We thank God for St. Mark and ask for his prayers.

title: The Agpeya and the seven prayers
text: The Agpeya is the Coptic book of the hours. It is our prayer book for seven times in the day, plus a Midnight prayer: Prime in the morning, Terce at the third hour, Sext at the sixth hour, None at the ninth hour, Vespers in the evening, and Compline before bed. Each hour remembers a moment in the life and suffering of Jesus, for example Prime remembers the Resurrection. Every hour has Psalms, a reading from the Gospel and short prayers. The idea of praying seven times a day comes from the Psalm that says, Seven times a day do I praise thee. A good start for a child is to pray Prime in the morning and Compline before bed. You do not have to pray all of them at once. Start small and grow slowly.

verse.text: Seven times a day do I praise thee

title: How do we pray?
text: Praying is simply talking and listening to God, like talking to a loving father. You can pray anywhere and at any time. Start by making the sign of the cross, thank God for good things, say sorry for anything you did wrong, and ask Him for help for yourself and others. Then say Amen. You can pray with your own words, with the Lord's Prayer, or with the prayers in the Agpeya. It is good to have a set time each day, like morning, before meals and before bed. You can stand, sit or kneel. God hears every prayer, even a very short one, and He loves to hear from you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Pray without ceasing.

title: What is fasting and why do we fast?
text: Fasting means going without some food, or not eating for a period of time, to grow closer to God. It is not a punishment and it is not a diet. In the Coptic Church fasting means giving up meat and other animal products like eggs, milk and cheese. We fast to strengthen our spiritual life and to give our minds and hearts more room for God. Fasting always goes together with prayer and repentance, and we offer it to God alone. Jesus fasted for forty days in the wilderness, and the apostles and the early Church also fasted. The rules for fasting are different for each person based on age and health, so kids should ask Abouna and their parents what is right for them.

title: Fasting on Wednesday and Friday
text: In the Coptic Church we fast on Wednesdays and Fridays during the year. This is a very old practice, and the early Church already kept these two days as fast days. We do not keep the Wednesday and Friday fast during the fifty days after the Resurrection, because that is a time of joy. On a fasting day we give up animal products, like meat, eggs, milk and cheese, and we pray more. The exact rules differ by age and health, and a priest can give an exception when someone needs it. Children should ask Abouna and their parents how much to fast.

title: The Great Lent
text: The Great Lent is the long fast before Easter, when we prepare to remember the death and Resurrection of Jesus. It lasts fifty-five days, and it is the longest fast of the year. It includes the forty days that follow the example of Jesus, who fasted forty days, and it ends with Holy Week. It is a time for more prayer, more kindness, more Bible reading and more giving. During Lent we give up meat and animal products and eat simple foods. A short three day fast, called the Fast of Nineveh, comes a couple of weeks before Lent. The Great Lent is not meant to be sad. It is a hopeful time as we walk with Jesus toward Pascha. Children should ask Abouna and parents what they can fast, since it depends on age and health.

title: The Coptic calendar and Nayrouz
text: The Coptic calendar is the calendar of the Coptic Church, and it comes from the ancient Egyptian calendar. It has thirteen months: twelve months of thirty days, and a little month at the end of five days, or six days in a leap year. The new year begins on the first day of the month of Tout, usually on 11 September. The feast of that day is called Nayrouz, a word that means the beginning of the year. Nayrouz is a day of joy, but the Church also remembers the martyrs, because the Coptic years are counted from the time of the martyrs. Many of our feasts and saint days are counted by the Coptic calendar. Ask Abouna to show you today's date in Coptic.

title: The Holy Family in Egypt
text: When Jesus was a little child, King Herod wanted to harm Him. An angel told Joseph in a dream to take Mary and Jesus and go to Egypt. So the Holy Family traveled to Egypt and stayed there until it was safe to go home. Because Jesus walked on the land of Egypt, the Coptic Church believes Egypt was blessed. The prophet Isaiah also said that the Lord would come to Egypt, and that there would be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt. We remember this journey every year, and we thank God for keeping Jesus safe. Many Egyptians love to visit the places where tradition says the Holy Family stayed.

title: Where did the Holy Family stay in Egypt?
text: Church tradition tells us that the Holy Family traveled through many places in Egypt, from the north of the country to the south, and that they were in Egypt for a number of years. Tradition remembers places such as Al-Mataria, Old Cairo, Wadi El Natrun and Al-Muharraq Monastery in Upper Egypt, where tradition says they stayed for a longer time. Many churches in these places honor the visit. Some details come from the tradition of the Church and not from the Bible, so the exact places and the length of time are told in different ways. The Coptic Church celebrates the entrance of the Holy Family into Egypt each year, and we remember it with thanks and joy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who are the martyrs?
text: A martyr is a person who loved Jesus so much that they never stopped believing in Him, even when other people were unkind or made things very hard for them. The word martyr means a witness. The first martyr was St. Stephen the deacon. Many Christians in Egypt were martyrs in the early years of the Church, and they stayed faithful to Jesus. We call them heroes of faith, and we believe they are alive with Christ and happy in heaven. We remember them in church and tell their stories, and we ask for their prayers. We can be brave and faithful like them, by being honest and standing up for what is right.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why does the Coptic calendar start from the Era of the Martyrs?
text: The Coptic calendar counts its years from the Era of the Martyrs, which is also called Anno Martyrum. It starts in the year 284 A.D., when the Roman emperor Diocletian came to the throne. During his rule many Christians in Egypt were put to death because they would not give up their faith. The Church chose to start counting from then to honor the martyrs and never forget how faithful they were. So the Coptic year number is lower than the regular year number by about 284 years. Counting this way is a way to say thank you to all those who held on to Christ through hard times.

title: What does Coptic mean?
text: The word Coptic comes from the Greek word for Egypt, and it came to mean the people and the church of Egypt. So the Coptic Church is the church of Egypt, and Copts are the Christians of Egypt. The Coptic language is the last stage of the ancient Egyptian language. It is written with the Greek alphabet plus some extra letters taken from the old Egyptian writing for sounds that Greek does not have. Arabic became the everyday language in Egypt many centuries ago, but Coptic is still the language of the Church, and it is used in the prayers and hymns. Some Copts today learn it again so they can pray in it.

title: Being ready for Holy Communion
text: Holy Communion is the Body and Blood of Jesus, so we get ready for it with care. We try to confess our sins to our priest and be truly sorry for what we did wrong. We make peace with anyone we have upset, because Jesus taught us to be reconciled with our brother before we come to the altar. In the Coptic Church we also fast before Communion, which means we do not eat or drink for a number of hours before we receive, and the length depends on age and health, so ask Abouna. We wash and come to church clean, listen to the Liturgy and pray with respect. If you are not sure whether you are ready, ask Abouna, and he will help you.

title: Saying sorry and being forgiven
text: Everyone makes mistakes, even grown ups. When we do something wrong, that is called sin. God does not want us to hide or feel afraid. He wants us to tell Him we are sorry and try again. This is called repentance. God is full of love, and He forgives us every time we ask from our heart. In confession, we tell our sins to God with Abouna listening, and Abouna prays that God forgives us. Then we feel light and clean. We should also forgive other people, the way God forgives us. Saying sorry is brave, and it makes us stronger and kinder.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

title: How should we behave in church?
text: The church is the house of God, so we come with joy and respect. We arrive on time, dress neatly, and turn off our phones. We make the sign of the cross when we enter and greet people kindly. During the service we listen, sing and pray, and we do not run, shout or play. We do not talk while the Gospel is read or during the prayers. If we need to leave, we do it quietly. When the Haykal curtain opens, we stay still and look at the altar. After the service we can greet Abouna and our friends. Kind and quiet behavior shows that we love Jesus and care for others.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Bible?
text: The Bible is God's Word, the holy book that tells us about God, His love and His plan to save us. It was written by many people over a long time, but they were inspired by the Holy Spirit. It has two big parts: the Old Testament and the New Testament. The Bible has stories, songs, laws, wise sayings and letters. We read it at home, in Sunday School and in the Liturgy, and the priest explains it. Reading a little each day helps us know God better. The Bible says that God's word is a lamp for our feet and a light for our path.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

title: The Old and New Testaments
text: The Bible has two parts. The Old Testament tells about the time before Jesus came. It has the stories of creation, Adam and Eve, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David and the prophets, and it has the Psalms and the books of wisdom. It points to Jesus who would come. The New Testament tells about the life of Jesus, the four Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, the Acts of the Apostles, the letters of the apostles and the Book of Revelation. The Old and New Testament belong together. The Coptic Church uses the full Old Testament, including the books that some churches leave out, and we read both in church.

title: Who are the angels?
text: Angels are spiritual beings that God created. They are not people who died, and we do not become angels. Angels worship God, bring His messages and take care of us. In the Bible the angel Gabriel told Mary she would have Jesus, and angels guarded people like Daniel. We know the names of the archangels Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, and we ask them to pray for us. Each person has a guardian angel, according to our Church tradition. We do not worship angels, we only worship God. When you feel scared, you can say a short prayer and remember that angels are near.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.

title: Who are the saints and why do we ask for their prayers?
text: Saints are people who loved God very much and lived holy lives. Now they are alive with Christ in heaven. The Church believes that they still care for us and pray for us. Just like we ask our parents or friends to pray for us, we ask the saints for their prayers. We do not pray to them as gods. We worship only God, and the saints help us by praying with us to Him. The saints include the apostles, the martyrs, the monks and many men and women of faith. We celebrate their feast days, read about their lives, and try to follow their good examples of love, courage and kindness.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Cross and Good Friday
text: Good Friday is the day Jesus died on the cross. He did this because He loves us, and He took our sins on Himself so that we could be forgiven and have life with God. It sounds sad, but it is also a day of great love. Jesus did not stay dead. He did this for us all. In the Coptic Church we call the week before Easter Holy Week, and on Good Friday we pray, read the Bible, sing sad hymns, and fast. We make the sign of the cross because the cross shows how much Jesus loves us. The cross is the sign of victory for Christians.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Resurrection
text: On the third day after Jesus died, He rose from the dead. This is the Resurrection, the greatest event in our faith. Early on Sunday morning, the women came to the tomb and found it empty, and an angel told them Jesus had risen. Then Jesus appeared to His disciples and many others, and they were filled with joy. By rising, Jesus defeated death and gave us hope of eternal life. We celebrate this at Easter, which we call the Feast of the Resurrection or Pascha, with a joyful Liturgy at night and a big family meal. We greet each other with Christ is risen, and answer, Truly He is risen.

verse.text: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.

title: How many sacraments are there?
text: The Coptic Orthodox Church has seven sacraments. A sacrament is a holy gift of God, where we receive His grace through the Church. The seven sacraments are Baptism, Chrismation with the Holy Myron, the Eucharist or Holy Communion, Repentance and Confession, the Unction of the Sick, Matrimony, and the Priesthood. Baptism and Chrismation are received one time. We can receive Communion and Confession many times. Each sacrament has its own card in Lumi, so you can ask about any of them.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who is St. Mark the Apostle?
text: St. Mark the Apostle brought the good news of Jesus to Egypt. He wrote the Gospel of Mark, and the Church teaches that he was the first Pope of Alexandria. That is why the Coptic Orthodox Church is called the Church of Alexandria, and why we are his spiritual children. Long ago he came to the great city of Alexandria, preached about Jesus, and many people believed and were baptized. He loved the people there, and he served them until the end of his life. Every time we go to church, we are part of the family that St. Mark began. We can thank God for him and ask for his prayers.

title: Who is St. Joseph the Carpenter?
text: St. Joseph was the righteous man who took care of St. Mary and baby Jesus. He worked hard as a carpenter. When an angel spoke to him in a dream, he listened to God and obeyed right away. He brought St. Mary and Jesus safely to Egypt, and later back home to Nazareth. He was gentle, quiet and trustworthy. The Church loves him as the guardian of the Holy Family. Joseph shows us that we can serve God by working honestly and by taking care of the people God gives us.

title: Who is St. John the Baptist?
text: St. John the Baptist was the cousin of Jesus. His parents were Zechariah and Elizabeth, and an angel told them about his birth. He lived simply and told people to turn back to God. His job was to get hearts ready for Jesus, so he is called the Forerunner. He baptized people in the Jordan River, and he baptized Jesus too. When he saw Jesus, he said Jesus is the Lamb of God. John was humble. He knew he was not the most important one, and he was happy to point to Jesus.

verse.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

title: Who is St. Stephen?
text: St. Stephen was one of the first seven deacons of the Church. He was full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and he helped take care of widows and people in need. He spoke boldly about Jesus. Some people did not like this, and in the end he gave his life for Jesus. He is called the first martyr. Even then he was gentle: he prayed that God would forgive the people who were unkind to him. The Church calls him the Archdeacon, and the deacons in our church ask for his prayers. Stephen shows us how to forgive.

title: Who is St. Peter the Apostle?
text: Peter was a fisherman called Simon. Jesus called him to follow Him and said, I will make you a fisher of men. Peter was one of the twelve apostles, and he was often the first to speak up. He loved Jesus very much, but once he was afraid and said he did not know Jesus. Jesus forgave him and loved him again. After Pentecost, Peter preached boldly and many people believed. His story tells us that when we make mistakes, we can say sorry, and Jesus forgives us. The Church remembers him together with St. Paul at the Feast of the Apostles.

title: Who is St. Paul the Apostle?
text: Paul was first called Saul. At first he was against the followers of Jesus. Then Jesus appeared to him on the road to Damascus, and his life changed completely. He was baptized and became a great apostle. Paul traveled to many countries to tell people about Jesus, and he started many churches. He also wrote letters to them, called epistles, and many are in the New Testament. Paul went through many hard times, but he kept trusting God. He teaches us that anyone can change and serve Jesus with all their heart.

title: Who is St. George?
text: St. George was born in Cappadocia, and when he grew up he went to the emperor's court to take his father's place. There he saw that the emperor had turned against Jesus and ordered everyone to worship idols. George felt sad. He gave his money to the poor and set his servants free. He said no to the emperor and stayed faithful to Jesus, and the Lord gave him strength. He was kind and he was not afraid. The Church calls him the Prince of Martyrs. Many pictures show him on a horse, and many churches in Egypt and around the world are named for him. When we feel afraid to do what is right, we can remember St. George and ask for his prayers.

title: Who is St. Mina the Wonder Worker?
text: St. Mina was born in Egypt, and his mother had prayed to God for a child. When he grew up he was given an important job in his city. When the emperor ordered everyone to worship idols, Mina left his job and went to the desert to pray for many days. Then he came back to the city and bravely said that he believed in Jesus. The Church calls him the Wonder Worker, because many people were helped and healed through his prayers. His body was laid to rest in the Mariout area near Alexandria, and a big monastery of St. Mina stands there today. Many Coptic children are named Mina. When we are sick or worried, we can ask St. Mina to pray for us.

title: Who is St. Antony the Great?
text: St. Antony is called the Father of Monks. As a young man he heard the Gospel in church and wanted to follow Jesus with his whole heart. He gave what he had to the poor and went to the desert to pray. He lived simply and spent his time with God. Many people came to ask him for advice, and many became monks because of him. He showed us that prayer is powerful and that God is with us even in lonely places. His monastery near the Red Sea is still alive today.

title: Who is St. Pachomius?
text: St. Pachomius was born in Thebes in Upper Egypt, to parents who did not know Jesus. They wanted him to worship idols, but he refused. When he grew up he became a monk and learned the monk's life from St. Balamon. Later an angel told him to start a life where monks live together. Many monks gathered around him, and he built monasteries for them. He gave them a plan for working, praying and eating together. This is called community life, so he is called the Father of Community Life. He led the monks for forty years. He teaches us that we are stronger when we love, share and help each other.

title: Who is St. Macarius the Great?
text: St. Macarius the Great was a monk who lived in the desert of Scetis in Wadi El Natrun in Egypt. He loved to pray and was known for his kindness and his patience. Many people came to learn from him, and they say he had a gentle heart. A famous monastery is named after him in the same desert, and monks still pray there today. He teaches us to be patient, to pray often and to speak kindly to everyone.

title: Who is St. Moses the Black?
text: St. Moses the Black lived in Egypt long ago. Before he became a monk he did many wrong things. Then he heard about God's love, he said sorry from his heart and went to live in the desert of Scetis. He worked hard to become gentle and humble, and many people learned from him. He is a wonderful example of repentance, which means turning back to God. No one is too far away for God to forgive, and we can always begin again.

title: Who is St. Bishoy?
text: St. Bishoy was born in a town called Shansa in Egypt. The story says his mother saw an angel in a dream, who asked her to give one of her children to serve God. The angel chose Bishoy, even though he was thin and small. When he grew up he went to the desert of Shiheet and became a monk. He prayed and worked very hard, and God made him worthy to see the Lord Jesus. He also found a simple way to teach about the Holy Trinity, using a basket with three ears. He is often called the Perfect Man because of his love. St. Bishoy teaches us to serve God with all our heart.

title: Who is St. Shenouda the Archimandrite?
text: St. Shenouda the Archimandrite was born near Akhmim in Upper Egypt. He became the leader of a large monastery after Anba Bgoul. He followed the rules for community life that St. Pachomius wrote, and he added a promise that each monk had to make before joining. So many monks came to live there that the number reached 2200. The word Archimandrite means leader of the monks. He also went with St. Cyril to the Council of Ephesus. Before he died, he told his disciples to follow his steps and trusted them to God. St. Shenouda shows us that praying, working and living together in love make a strong family.

title: Who is St. Demiana?
text: St. Demiana lived in Egypt and gave her life to Jesus. She was the daughter of a governor, and she gathered forty young women who prayed and served God together with her. They were brave and loved each other, and they stayed faithful to Jesus even in hard times. The Church remembers them on the 13th of Tobi. There is a famous monastery of St. Demiana in the Delta, and many girls in Egypt are named after her. Their story shows us that good friends help each other love God.

title: Who is Archangel Michael?
text: The Archangel Michael is one of God's great angels. Angels are God's servants who are sent to help us. Michael is known as the protector of God's people, and the Church asks for his prayers every month on the 12th of the Coptic month. In the Bible he is a leader who stands up for the good. We cannot see angels, but God sends them to take care of us. We can pray, Archangel Michael, please pray for us, and we do not need to be afraid.

title: Who is Archangel Gabriel?
text: The Archangel Gabriel is the angel who brings good news. God sent him to tell Zechariah that he would have a son named John. Then God sent him to St. Mary in Nazareth to tell her that she would be the mother of Jesus. He said, Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you. We remember his message every year at the Feast of the Annunciation. God sends us good news too, in the Bible and in prayer.

title: Who is St. Athanasius the Apostolic?
text: St. Athanasius was the 20th Pope of Alexandria, and he is called the Apostolic because he held to the faith of the apostles. When he was a young deacon, he went with his Pope to the Council of Nicea. There the Church taught clearly that Jesus Christ is truly God. Athanasius kept teaching this faith, even when powerful people were against him and he was sent away several times. Because of him, the Church is strong in the true faith. He teaches us to stand for what is true with love and courage.

title: Who is St. Cyril the Great?
text: St. Cyril was the 24th Pope of Alexandria and is called the Pillar of the Faith. He defended the teaching that St. Mary is truly the Theotokos, which means the Mother of God, because the child she carried is God the Son. This was affirmed at the Council of Ephesus. Cyril wrote many books explaining the faith, and the Church still loves them. When we sing praises to St. Mary, we remember how Cyril and the Church honored her.

title: Who is St. Mary of Egypt?
text: St. Mary of Egypt lived long ago. In her young life she was far from God. Then, during a visit to Jerusalem, she was moved to pray and she decided to change. She went into the desert beyond the Jordan River and lived there in prayer for many years. A priest named Zosimas met her near the end of her life. The Church remembers her on the 6th of Baramouda. St. Mary of Egypt reminds us that no matter what has happened, God welcomes everyone who turns back to Him with all their heart.

title: Who is St. Abanoub?
text: St. Abanoub was a young boy who loved Jesus very much. He was born in the town of Nehisa in Egypt, and his parents taught him to love God and to be kind.
